core_meaning.short_meaning: Continuous devotion, acts of worship; major companion Ubadah ibn al-Samit.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Ubadah (عُبَادَة) is an Arabic masculine given name meaning 'profound devotion', 'constant worship', or 'servitude to the Divine'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Ubadah ibn al-Samit al-Ansari, a chieftain of the Khazraj, leader at both Pledges of Aqaba, and premier teacher of the Quran in the Levant.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Derived from ʿibādah (worship), expressing a life steeped in divine adoration, humility, and steadfast obedience to Allah.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root ʿ-b-d denotes devotion, submission, and worship of Allah alone. Ubadah ibn al-Samit was one of the twelve chieftains (Nuqaba) chosen at the Second Pledge of Aqaba. He fought at Badr, collected and memorized the Quran, and was sent by Umar ibn al-Khattab as teacher and chief judge to Palestine, where he lived with uncompromising righteousness until his death in Ramla.

faq.a: Ubadah (عُبَادَة) is an Arabic masculine given name meaning 'profound devotion', 'constant worship', or 'servitude to the Divine'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Ubadah ibn al-Samit al-Ansari, a chieftain of the Khazraj, leader at both Pledges of Aqaba, and premier teacher of the Quran in the Levant.

faq.q: What is the origin of Ubadah?
faq.a: The root ʿ-b-d denotes devotion, submission, and worship of Allah alone. Ubadah ibn al-Samit was one of the twelve chieftains (Nuqaba) chosen at the Second Pledge of Aqaba. He fought at Badr, collected and memorized the Quran, and was sent by Umar ibn al-Khattab as teacher and chief judge to Palestine, where he lived with uncompromising righteousness until his death in Ramla.
Yes. The recorded language/origin is Arabic; the source form is عُبَادَة.

faq.q: How is Ubadah written in Arabic?

faq.a: It is not claimed as a Qur'anic personal name. The personal name Ubadah is not in the Quran; its triliteral root ʿ-b-d forms the very core of Quranic monotheistic worship (e.g. 1:5, 51:56).

Name of an illustrious Companion revered for his spiritual mastery, profound knowledge of the Quran, and uncompromising defense of truth. Named after Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who swore never to fear the reproach of any faultfinder in speaking the truth for the sake of Allah.
An approximate romanized guide is oo-BAA-dah. Initial pharyngeal 'ʿayn' followed by long vowel 'baa' and soft final 'dah'.

faq.a: The documented naming sources record Ubadah as a male name; actual use can vary by language and community.
